messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. We need to interpret what they mean. Possibly they have a momentum vector and want to find the angle of the force vector? Or maybe they want to find the angle between force and momentum? The question is ambiguous. But we can provide general guidance: Force is the time derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. So if you know momentum as a function of time, differentiate to get force. Then find angle of force vector relative to some axis using arctan2 or similar. Use the function calculate_vector_angle to compute angle from components. Provide example code. Also mention that if momentum is constant, force is zero. Provide steps: 1) Determine momentum components p_x, p_y. 2) Compute derivatives dp_x/dt, dp_y/dt to get force components. 3) Use arctan2 to find angle. Provide formula: angle = atan2(F_y, F_x). Use degrees if needed. Provide example: Suppose momentum p = (p_x, p_y). Then F = (dp_x/dt, dp_y/dt). Then angle = atan2(dp_y/dt, dp_x/dt). Provide code snippet. Also mention that if momentum is given as magnitude and direction, you can convert to components first. Provide explanation. Also mention that if you only have magnitude of momentum and want angle of force relative to momentum, you can use dot product: cos(theta) = (F·p)/(||F|| ||p||). But likely they want angle of force vector. Provide both possibilities.

We should also call the function calculate_vector_angle with sample values. For demonstration, we can assume some numeric example: Suppose F_x=3 N, F_y=4 N. Then angle = arctan2(4,3) ~ 53.13 degrees. Use function. We'll call it.
